title: SDK disconnected developer loop and fallback playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook explains recommended developer-experience patterns for working when a developer is disconnected from Redwood hosted services (air-gapped or flaky network), and for building deterministic fallback behaviors in client SDKs. It covers local stubs, deterministic replay, telemetry contracts, and a short set of canonical fixes for the highest-frequency support issues we see in this space.

Audience: SDK authors, integrators, platform engineers, solutions engineers, and support engineers.

Goals
- Enable reproducible local development when the host API is unavailable.
- Ensure clear, actionable telemetry even during local/offline flows.
- Provide canonical fallback logic so product code degrades gracefully and support triage is fast.

Quick summary of recommended patterns
1) Local stub server + recorded responses (golden corpus).
2) Deterministic prompt bundling and replay for offline tests.
3) Local quota/usage simulation to exercise cost controls.
4) Telemetry shim that annotates whether a response was live, cached, or simulated.
5) Graceful API fallback surface area: short-circuit, best-effort cached response, reduced-functionality response, user-visible fallback message.

Prerequisites
- Developer machine with Docker (for local stub).
- A small "golden" test corpus of prompt/response pairs kept per-integration. See the template below.
- Access to the SDK debug flags (ENABLE_LOCAL_STUB, TELEMETRY_MODE).

Quickstart: local disconnected loop (3 steps)
1) Install local stub container
   - docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/local-stub:stable
2) Point SDK to local endpoint
   - export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-goldencorp-key
3) Run the deterministic replay test
   - python tests/replay_test.py --corpus=golden/reply-corpus.json --verify-sigs

Templates and examples
- Golden corpus format (JSON; simplified):
  [
    {
      "id": "greeting-001",
      "input": "Write a short onboarding welcome for a new user named Ana.",
      "model": "rwd-3-small",
      "response": "Welcome Ana! We're excited to have you...",
      "tags": ["smoke", "greeting"]
    }
  ]

- SDK config snippet (env-driven)
  REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-goldencorp-key
  REDWOOD_SDK_FALLBACK_STRATEGY=cached_then_reduced
  REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=shim

- Python example: deterministic replay harness (pseudo)
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(base_url=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_URL'))
  for item in load_corpus('golden/reply-corpus.json'):
      r = c.generate(prompt=item['input'], model=item['model'])
      assert normalize(r.text) == normalize(item['response'])

API examples and canonical behaviors
- Live -> Cached fallback (preferred): If live call fails with a 5xx or network error within 300 ms, return cached response with metadata flag "fallback_source":"cache" and telemetry.event=fallback_cache_returned.
- Live -> Reduced feature response: If the requested structured output (tools/function-calls) is unsupported locally, return an abbreviated JSON with fields: {"ok": false, "reason": "reduced_features", "partial_text": "..."}.
- Circuit-breaker: After 5 consecutive remote failures, SDK should trip for 60s and return cached or reduced responses. Telemetry must include circuit_breaker_status.

Observability & telemetry contract (required fields)
Telemetry event schema must include the following tags for offline/fallback flows:
- event_type: one of [request_start, request_end, fallback_used, cache_hit, circuit_tripped]
- request_id: developer-visible request id
- fallback_source: one of [none, cache, local_sim, reduced]
- simulated: boolean (true for local simulated responses)
- latency_ms: integer (if simulated, set to 0)
- sdk_version: string
- local_stub_id: optional string (if using local stub)

Please ensure telemetry is batched and sent only when network is available; include a persistent local buffer with size cap 10MB and an eviction policy.

Common support issues and canonical fixes (top 6 for disconnected flows)
1) Symptom: SDK returns a stale cached response with no metadata.
   Canonical fix: Ensure all cached responses include headers: X-RWD-Fallback: cache; X-RWD-Cached-At: <ISO8601>. Add unit tests that assert these headers are present.
2) Symptom: Replay tests fail due to small whitespace/tokenization differences.
   Canonical fix: Use normalize() helper (strip, collapse whitespace, canonicalize punctuation) in both golden corpus generation and tests. Document tokenization caveats for rwd-3-small in the golden corpus README.
3) Symptom: Telemetry shows missing request_id for simulated responses.
   Canonical fix: Always synthesize request_id using prefix "local-" + sha256(input + model + timestamp).
4) Symptom: SDK circuit-breaker trips but never recovers.
   Canonical fix: Implement half-open probe after cooldown: send single low-QPS health check and clear circuit if successful. Telemetry: emit circuit_probe_result.
5) Symptom: Users see UI-level "Service unavailable" when reduced-mode would be better.
   Canonical fix: Default fallback route should be cached_then_reduced (see SDK config) and UI should render partial_text when ok=false and reason=reduced_features.
6) Symptom: Local stub drift (golden corpus outdated).
   Canonical fix: Add daily CI job that runs a lightweight smoke test against the latest model snapshot and flags corpus mismatches for review.

Runbook: triage steps for an offline-related support ticket
1) Confirm whether caller used local stub or remote API (check telemetry.fallback_source).
2) If fallback_source==cache, fetch cached payload and validate X-RWD-Cached-At header and SIG.
3) If simulated, check local-stub-id and developer environment variables; ask for golden corpus hash.
4) If circuit_tripped, check consecutive failure metrics and recent probe results. Reset circuit only after reproducing success.
5) If mismatch to golden corpus, request developer to run the provided normalize-and-diff tool and attach output.

Deployment and rollout checklist for SDK authors
- Add ENABLE_LOCAL_STUB and TELEMETRY_MODE flags behind a feature gate.
- Add unit tests for: cache header presence, request_id synthesis, circuit breaker probe behavior, telemetry schema conformance.
- Document how to create and update golden corpus (include generator tool).
- Add CI job that runs replay tests against host environment for smoke coverage.

Ownership and escalation
- SDK runtime: devx-sdk-team@redwood.internal (primary).
- Support escalation: devx-oncall@redwood.internal (secondary).
- Golden corpus curation: solutions-eng-team (curation cadence: weekly).

Related resources
- Local stub image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/local-stub:stable
- Telemetry spec: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-telemetry-spec-2025
- Replay tooling repo: internal git: github.com/redwood/devx/replay-harness

Appendix: small decision log entries
- 2025-10-12: Chose "cached_then_reduced" as default because it minimizes user-visible failure while preserving deterministic behavior for tests.
- 2025-11-01: Require persistent local telemetry buffer size cap 10MB to limit local disk use.
